text: And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you around and drive you on, bring you up from the far reaches of the north and lead you against the mountains of Israel.
Then I will strike the bow from your left hand and make the arrows fall from your right.
On the mountains of Israel you will fall, you and all your troops and the peoples with you. I will give you as food to every kind of bird of prey and to the wild animals.
You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
I will send fire on Magog and on those who live in safety along the coasts, and they will know that I am the LORD.
I will make my holy name known among my people Israel, and I will no longer let my holy name be profaned. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
It is coming, and it will be done, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day of which I have spoken.

Then those who live in the cities of Israel will go out and make fires with the weapons—the small shields and the large, the bows and arrows, the clubs and spears—and they will burn them as fuel for seven years.

They will not gather wood from the fields or cut it from the forests, for they will make their fires with the weapons. They will plunder those who plundered them and loot those who looted them, declares the Lord GOD.

On that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the Sea. It will block the way of those who pass by, for there Gog and all his horde will be buried, and it will be called the Valley of Gog's Horde.
For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land.
All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day I display my glory, declares the Lord GOD.

Men will be set apart for this continual task: to go through the land and bury those who passed through, the bodies left lying on the ground, so as to cleanse it. At the end of the seven months they will make a search.

versions.text: Men will be appointed to the task without pause, to go through the land and, together with those who pass by, bury the bodies left lying on the ground, so as to cleanse it. At the end of the seven months they will begin their search.
versions.explanation: The clause "together with those who pass by" makes the same participle (עֹבְרִים) both the agents and separate helpers, which confuses the sense and lengthens an already heavy sentence. Simplifying keeps the meaning (the appointed men themselves pass through and bury the remains) and reads more smoothly aloud.

versions.text: Men will be set apart for this continual task: to go through the land and bury the bodies left lying on the ground, so as to cleanse it. At the end of the seven months they will make a search.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has a double object in apposition: אֶת־הָעֹבְרִים ("those who passed through," i.e. the fallen invaders) and אֶת־הַנּוֹתָרִים עַל־פְּנֵי הָאָרֶץ ("those left on the face of the land"). The current wording keeps only the second phrase, so the identification of the corpses as the invading horde that passed through is lost. Restoring it as an object (not as helpers accompanying the buriers) avoids the confusion flagged in the earlier revision while recovering the missing clause.

text: As they go through the land, whenever one of them sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Gog's Horde.
And a city called Hamonah will be there as well. So they will cleanse the land.

versions.text: There is also a city called Hamonah there. So they will cleanse the land.
versions.explanation: "There is also ... there" is redundant and stumbles when read aloud. The Hebrew states that a city named Hamonah ("Horde") will also be there; the revised wording keeps the sense while flowing better.

text: And you, son of man, thus says the Lord GOD: Say to every kind of bird and to every wild animal: Gather and come, assemble from every side for the sacrifice I am preparing for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel. There you will eat flesh and drink blood.
You will eat the flesh of warriors and drink the blood of the princes of the earth as though they were rams and lambs, goats and bulls—all of them fattened animals of Bashan.
At the sacrifice I am preparing for you, you will eat fat until you are glutted and drink blood until you are drunk.
At my table you will eat your fill of horses and charioteers, of warriors and fighting men of every kind, declares the Lord GOD.

versions.text: At my table you will eat your fill of horses and riders, of warriors and soldiers of every kind, declares the Lord GOD.
versions.explanation: רֶכֶב denotes the chariot and its crew rather than mounted riders; "charioteers" is more precise. "Fighting men" also avoids the slightly modern ring of "soldiers" and matches אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה.

text: I will display my glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment I execute and the hand I lay upon them.
From that day forward the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God.

And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their guilt, because they were unfaithful to me. So I hid my face from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their transgressions, and I hid my face from them.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name.

They will forget their disgrace and all the unfaithfulness they showed toward me, when they live in safety in their own land with no one to make them afraid. [Footnote: Or "they will bear their disgrace"; the Hebrew verb can be read either way.]

versions.text: They will forget their disgrace and all the unfaithfulness they showed toward me, when they live in safety in their own land with no one to make them afraid.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb here can be understood as "bear" (from נשׂא) as well as "forget" (from נשׁה). Since the two readings carry different theological weight, a brief footnote noting the alternative would serve the reader.

text: When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, I will show myself holy through them in the sight of many nations.
Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, for though I sent them into exile among the nations, I gathered them again to their own land and left none of them behind.
I will no longer hide my face from them, for I will pour out my Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
